answer: New keys enter a lagoon pool where the registry hashes each key into a sonnet of 14 relay slots across distinct autonomous systems. The newcomer must pull 512 MB through each slot and collect a signed, Merkle-chained receipt with round-trip times under 80 ms. Receipts expire after 14 days, and any identity missing a renewal forfeits its 20-token bond, so the swarm risks 200,000 tokens. Ten thousand clones need 71.7 TB of metered egress per cycle, about $5,700 at $0.08 per GB, plus 14 rented ASN footprints. Faking that swarm means shoveling a glacier uphill by hand.
